card.name: Adverbs like too, all, as before time words
card.fires_on: Small adverbs or linking words such as too, all, as, every, right that come after a clause and just before a time or degree phrase like quickly, year, soon as possible, time, away.

modes.label: Degree/time adverb
modes.description: The word too, as or right begins a phrase about speed or lateness.
modes.example: far<< too>> late to make any difference to the economy

modes.label: Coverage of all times
modes.description: The word all or every comes before time words like year, things, or time, meaning always.
modes.example: aim for 100% ground cover<< all>> year, with a focus on perennial grass

modes.label: Comma after a broad noun
modes.description: A comma or period after everyone or anything, before an added phrase like anytime.
modes.example: We have unprecedented power to map anything<<,>> anytime.

card.writes: It favors words meaning always or everywhere (forever, anytime, throughout) and suppresses odd word-pieces.
card.plain: It marks a small word that is about to be followed by a time or extent phrase such as all year, too late, or as soon as possible.
